title: Claude Opus 5
content:
## Overview

Claude Opus 5 is Anthropic's latest top-tier model, released **July 24, 2026**. It is positioned as a frontier-class model for agentic coding and computer use, and notably ships at the **same price as its predecessor, Opus 4.8**, despite a large jump in benchmark scores. It immediately became the default model on Claude Max and the strongest available option on Claude Pro.

---

## Key Specs

| Spec | Value |
|---|---|
| Release date | July 24, 2026 |
| Context window | 1M tokens |
| Max output | 128K tokens |
| Knowledge cutoff | May 2026 |
| Pricing | $5 / $25 per million input/output tokens (unchanged from Opus 4.8) |

That pricing is exactly **half the cost** of Claude Fable 5, Anthropic's other current flagship-class model, while landing close to it on several agentic benchmarks.

---

## Benchmark Highlights

- **Frontier-Bench v0.1:** Opus 5 more than doubles Opus 4.8's score and leads all other models on the benchmark.
- **CursorBench 3.2** (agentic coding): Opus 5 lands within 0.5% of Fable 5's peak score, at half the per-task cost.
- **ARC-AGI 3:** Opus 5 scores roughly 3x the next-best model, the largest single-generation jump reported so far on this benchmark.
- **OSWorld 2.0** (computer use): Opus 5 surpasses Fable 5's best recorded result while costing just over a third as much per run.

The pattern echoes what happened with Claude 3.5 Sonnet in 2024 — a mid-cycle release outperforming a more expensive sibling model — except this time it's the Opus tier itself leapfrogging on cost-efficiency rather than a cheaper tier catching up.

---

## New Capabilities

- **Frontier-class agentic coding:** Opus 5 is tuned specifically for long-horizon coding tasks (large refactors, multi-file changes, autonomous debugging loops), building on the agentic focus introduced in the Claude 4 generation.
- **Computer use improvements:** Faster and more reliable GUI automation compared to Opus 4.8, narrowing the gap with Fable 5 on OSWorld 2.0 while remaining cheaper to run.
- **Beta: mid-conversation tool changes** — the ability to add or remove available tools partway through a conversation without restarting the session.
- **Beta: automatic API fallbacks** — requests can automatically retry against a fallback model/region on transient failures, improving reliability for production agent deployments.

---

## Where It Fits in the Lineup

As of August 2026, Anthropic's active model lineup is:

- **Claude Fable 5** — the highest-capability, highest-cost flagship
- **Claude Opus 5** — near-flagship performance at half of Fable 5's price
- **Claude Sonnet 5** — balanced, general-purpose workhorse
- **Claude Haiku 4.5** — fastest and cheapest tier
- **Claude Mythos 5** — restricted-access model (limited availability)

This breaks from the traditional Haiku/Sonnet/Opus-only structure used since Claude 3 (2024): Opus is no longer strictly Anthropic's most expensive tier, since Fable 5 now sits above it on both price and (narrowly) capability.

---

## Why It Matters

Opus 5's release continues a consistent trend across Claude generations: each new release pushes the previous generation's top-tier capability down to a lower price point. For teams building agentic coding tools, the combination of a 1M-token context window, frontier-level CursorBench performance, and unchanged Opus pricing makes it a notable default upgrade candidate for cost-sensitive production agents.
